bridge: Builds on D08 decisions, P04 timestamp normalisation and C06 files. This workshop supplies a small evidence packet instead of assuming an unavailable disk image.
teaching:
Forensics asks what a set of artifacts supports and how reliably it was preserved. Keep originals unchanged, analyse copies and record provenance. A cryptographic hash can detect byte changes relative to a trusted recorded hash; it does not by itself prove who created the artifact or whether its contents are true.

Timestamps have sources and semantics. File creation, modification, access and collection times are different. Clock offsets, copied files and missing logs can alter interpretations. Corroborate an event across independent sources where possible and distinguish a user account label from proof of a particular human actor.

The supplied packet is intentionally text-only so it can be reproduced on any platform. It is not a full disk or packet image. Advanced acquisition, registry and packet analysis remains in the assigned readings; do not claim those skills were demonstrated solely by this small timeline.

Treat the demonstration as evidence interpretation on a particular Windows version. Preserve the original image or collection, parse a working copy, and record tool and operating-system versions. A registry key’s last-write timestamp is not automatically the time a file was created, first opened or copied. A recent-document entry may reflect an application interaction without proving which person read its contents. Check the time format and timezone for each artifact instead of assuming every Windows timestamp follows one rule. Do not assume that RegBack contains automatic backups on a current installation. Select the offline control set from the SYSTEM hive evidence rather than assuming ControlSet001 was active.
example:
Save these three UTF-8 files exactly (one line each).
file-record.txt:
F1,note.txt,modified,2026-01-01T10:00:00+01:00
endpoint-record.txt:
E1,account-A,wrote-note,2026-01-01T09:00:00+00:00
network-record.txt:
N1,host-H,connected-docs,2026-01-01T09:02:00+00:00

Collection manifest: source=synthetic workshop; collector=your practice name;
record your actual collection time, tool version and SHA-256 for each file.
explanation: F1 and E1 describe matching instants after offset conversion and can corroborate the stated write at the fixture level. N1 shows a later connection, not the content of a transfer. Save your own computed hashes; they depend on exact bytes and newline conventions, so a fixed universal digest is not supplied.
exercise: Create all three files, hash originals using Python hashlib or your documented system tool, copy them to an analysis folder and verify hashes match. Build a UTC timeline and write one supported claim, one inference and two unknowns.
solution:
Create the three named source files in a fresh practice folder, with only their one record each. Then run this script there; it copies only the three explicitly named local files.

```python
import hashlib
from pathlib import Path
from shutil import copyfile
names = ["file-record.txt", "endpoint-record.txt", "network-record.txt"]
analysis = Path("analysis")
analysis.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
for name in names:
    original = Path(name)
    digest = hashlib.sha256(original.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    copied = analysis / name
    copyfile(original, copied)
    same = hashlib.sha256(copied.read_bytes()).hexdigest() == digest
    print(name, digest, "copy matches:", same)
```

Record all three digests and confirm True for each copy. Keep the collection metadata separately and analyse only copies. UTC timeline: F1 and E1 at 09:00, N1 at 09:02. Supported claim: the supplied records describe a matching file modification and account write time. Inference: they may refer to the same write. Unknowns include the human actor and any transferred contents. Matching times alone do not prove causation or exfiltration.
challenge: In an analysis copy only, change N1 to 09:01 UTC and recompute its hash. Explain the integrity result and whether F1/E1 establish that note contents were exported over the network.
challenge_solution: The modified copy's hash differs from its baseline. This detects a byte change but does not attribute it by itself. Matching file/write times do not prove network exfiltration. A report must retain originals, disclose modification and bound conclusions.
